name: htmlradar-mcp

tools.name: share_html
tools.description: Publishes an HTML document — a deck, report, dashboard, proposal or one-pager — as a tracked HTMLRadar link, and returns two addresses: the link for the recipient, and a dashboard address for the sender. The recipient sees the document as written and never the tracking. The markup goes in `html`; there is no file-path argument, so a document on disk reaches this tool only as markup the caller has already read, which leaves the user's permissions on their own file tools in charge of what is published. By default the recipient is asked for their email address before the document opens, which is a step the person receiving the link has to take. The link is live the moment it is returned. The answer includes the saved rules and comments state. Images that need a login, expiring image addresses and local file paths do not load for readers of the link. Images embedded in the HTML as data URIs always do. On an update, get_document shows each embedded image as a short htmlradar-image reference; keep each one exactly as it is and HTMLRadar puts the image back, so only new images count towards the 5 MB limit.

html.description: The HTML markup to publish, in full. There is no file-path argument: a document on disk reaches this tool only as markup the caller has already read.

title.description: Name shown on your dashboard. Recipients do not see it.

comments.description: Whether readers can comment. Off by default. Turning comments on needs the email gate and a one-time code; who sees comments follows the link.

recipient_label.description: Who this link is for, e.g. "Acme". One link per recipient reads best.

require_email.description: Ask the recipient for their email before the document opens. Defaults to true.

verify_email.description: Verify that the address really is the reader's: we email a six-digit code and open the document only when the reader types it back. Off by default. Use it when the list of who opened the document has to be true rather than merely typed. Needs the email gate, which is on by default; with it off the call is refused.

password.description: Extra password gate on top of the email gate.

lock_deck.description: Blocks save and print and adds a watermark; default true. Pass false for a document the recipient is meant to keep a copy of.

allowed_email_domains.description: Only these email domains may open the link, e.g. ["acme.com"]. Up to 500. Needs the email gate, which is on by default; with it off the call is refused.

allowed_emails.description: Only these exact addresses may open the link, e.g. ["ravi@acme.com"]. A separate list from the domains, and a visitor passes on either. Up to 500 addresses; past that a domain is the right tool. Needs the email gate, which is on by default; with it off the call is refused.

expires_in_hours.description: Link stops working after this many hours.

slug.description: Custom link name, so the URL reads /r/acme-proposal. Paid plans only.

request_id.description: Leave unset on a first attempt. When a previous call failed saying it may still have been applied, pass the request_id that error named: the retry then returns the first result instead of doing it twice.

annotations.title: Share HTML as a tracked link

tools.name: create_share
tools.description: Creates an additional tracked link for a document already on HTMLRadar, with its own recipient label, gate, password, expiry and address. One link per recipient is what separates their reading reports. It uploads nothing and creates no second copy of the document, and it cannot publish new markup: it takes a document id, which list_shares returns and share_html returned when the document was first published. The link is live the moment it is returned. The answer includes the saved rules and comments state.

document_id.description: The document to make another link for — the document id from list_shares, or the one share_html returned when the document was first published.

tools.name: list_shares
tools.description: Lists the account's tracked links, newest first: the slug, the recipient label, the document title, whether it has been opened and when, and the share and document ids the other tools take. This is where the identifiers for a link made in an earlier conversation come from. The `opened` and `last_open` fields answer "which of my links has nobody opened" on their own, without a get_share_activity report for each one. Returns at most 50 per call; the `before` cursor pages back through older links.

before.description: Cursor for the next page: the `next_before` value printed at the end of a previous list_shares result, of the form <created_at>|<share id>. Pass it back exactly as printed. Omit for the most recent links.

annotations.title: List tracked links on this account

tools.name: list_documents
tools.description: Lists the account's documents, newest first: the title, when it was created, how many tracked links point at it, and the document id that create_share and replace_document take. A document with no links appears here and nowhere else, because list_shares only knows documents that have been sent. It returns no document contents. Returns at most 50 per call; the `before` cursor pages back through older documents.

before.description: Cursor for the next page: the `next_before` value printed at the end of a previous list_documents result, of the form <created_at>|<document id>. Pass it back exactly as printed. Omit for the most recent documents.

tools.name: get_share_activity
tools.description: Reports whether a tracked HTMLRadar link has been opened, by whom, for how long, how far they scrolled, and which sections held their attention. Per viewer it names the all recorded sections, ordered by reading time. Reading times are rounded down; scroll percentages are rounded to the nearest whole percent. It accepts a share id, a slug or a link; list_shares returns all three.

share_id.description: The share id returned by share_html, or the share's slug (the part after /r/ in its link), or the link itself.

include_detail.description: Also return each reader's country, city, device and referrer. Off by default: that is a named person's location and device, and whether the document was read and which parts of it is answered without them.

annotations.title: Check who read a tracked link

tools.name: revoke_share
tools.description: Switches off a tracked link that has already been sent. Anyone who opens it afterwards sees that it is no longer available, and the sender is emailed that somebody tried. This changes what a recipient can see. It is reversible — `revoked: false` switches the link back on, so use this tool to turn a switched-off link on again — and it deletes nothing: the link, its settings and its whole reading history survive. Deleting a link is possible only on the website, because it deletes its reading records for good. To change a link's settings, use update_share on the same link: switching one off to make a replacement leaves the recipient holding a dead address.

share_id.description: The share id, the share's slug (the part after /r/ in its link), or the link itself. list_shares returns all three.

revoked.description: True (the default) switches the link off. False switches it back on.

annotations.title: Switch a tracked link off, or back on

tools.name: get_share
tools.description: Returns a tracked link's current settings, in the form update_share changes them: who can open it (the full allowed-domain and allowed-address lists), the email gate and its one-time code, whether a password is set (never the password), the end date, the copy lock, comments, the label, who the gate names, whether the sender is emailed on the first open, and the settings version. It reads one of this account's links and changes nothing. The answer includes the saved Rules line and the version used by expected_settings_version.

share_id.description: The share id, the share's slug (the part after /r/ in its link), or the link itself. list_shares returns all three.

tools.name: update_share
tools.description: Changes the settings of a tracked link that has already been sent, on the same link: who can open it (allowed domains and addresses), the email gate and its one-time code, the password, the end date, the copy lock, the label, who the gate names and whether the sender is emailed on the first open. Comments can be on or off; enabling needs a code-confirmed email gate. The answer includes the saved Rules line. The link, its address and its whole reading history stay the same. Only the settings you name change; every other setting is left as it is, and a setting is removed only when it is named in `clear`. The list arguments add_allowed_emails, remove_allowed_emails, add_allowed_email_domains and remove_allowed_email_domains: the server merges them over the stored list and says what was added, removed and not found. Sending allowed_emails or allowed_email_domains replaces the whole list and needs expected_settings_version from get_share, so a change made since is never overwritten. A stale version is refused without saving. A change applies from the next time the page is loaded: someone reading it right now keeps the page they have until they reload. If the sender is on a company team, the team's rules apply to this change exactly as on the website (for example a required one-time code or company domains), and a change that breaks one is refused with the rule named. Narrowing who can open a link, or removing a list, changes what recipients can see.

comments.description: Whether readers can comment. Omitted keeps the current choice. Turning comments on needs the email gate and a one-time code; who sees comments follows the link.

share_id.description: The share id, the share's slug (the part after /r/ in its link), or the link itself. list_shares returns all three.

recipient_label.description: A new label for who this link is for, e.g. "Acme".

require_email.description: Turn the email gate on or off. Turning it off removes the check that the list of allowed domains and addresses relies on, so clear those in the same call.

verify_email.description: Turn the one-time-code check on or off: we email the reader a six-digit code and open the document only when they type it back. Needs the email gate on.

password.description: Set a password (at least 8 characters) on top of the email gate. To remove one, use `clear`.

lock_deck.description: The copy lock: true blocks save and print and adds a watermark; false allows them.

allowed_email_domains.description: Only these email domains may open the link, e.g. ["acme.com"]. This REPLACES the whole stored list: call get_share first and send the domains that should stay with the new one. To remove the list, use `clear`. Needs the email gate on.

allowed_emails.description: Only these exact addresses may open the link. A separate list from the domains; a visitor passes on either. This REPLACES the whole stored list: call get_share first and send the addresses that should stay with the new one. To remove the list, use `clear`. Needs the email gate on.

add_allowed_emails.description: Addresses to ADD to the stored list of allowed addresses. The server merges them over the list as it is now, so nothing has to be copied back. Needs the email gate on.

remove_allowed_emails.description: Addresses to REMOVE from the stored list of allowed addresses. The answer says which were not on the list. Removing the last entry of every list is refused; use `clear` for that.

add_allowed_email_domains.description: Domains to ADD to the stored list of allowed domains, merged on the server.

remove_allowed_email_domains.description: Domains to REMOVE from the stored list of allowed domains, merged on the server.

expected_settings_version.description: The settings version get_share showed. The change is made only if the link is still at that version; otherwise nothing is changed and you are told to call get_share again. Required when you replace or clear a whole list (allowed_emails, allowed_email_domains).

expires_at.description: When the link stops working, as a date and time such as 2026-12-31T17:00:00Z. Give this or `expires_in_hours`. To remove the end date, use `clear`.

expires_in_hours.description: The link stops working this many hours from now. Give this or `expires_at`.

show_sender.description: Who the gate names to the reader: nobody, the sender's company, or the sender's name. The company needs a work sign-up address; the name needs one set in Settings.

notify_first_open.description: Whether the sender is emailed when someone first opens this link.

clear.description: Settings to remove: the label, the password, the end date, the domain list, the address list. Removing a list lets anyone who passes the email gate in, so say so to the user first. A setting that is not named here or above is left exactly as it is.

tools.name: list_attachments
tools.description: Lists the files attached to a document on HTMLRadar (supporting materials a reader can download beside the page): the file name, its size and the attachment id that remove_attachment takes. It returns no file contents and changes nothing. Call it before add_attachment or remove_attachment, and after an add that failed without an answer.

document_id.description: The document — the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

tools.name: add_attachment
tools.description: Attaches one file to a document already on HTMLRadar, for readers of its links to download. The file types are the website's (PDF, Office documents, images, CSV, text, Markdown, ZIP) and a document holds up to 20 files. The file travels as base64 in `content_base64`, because a tool argument is JSON, so it can be at most 5.0 MB, the same limit as publishing a page this way; a larger file (the website takes 25 MB) is added on the website. Readers see the file from the next time they load the page. There is no file-path argument: a file on disk reaches this tool only as content the caller has already read.

document_id.description: The document — the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

filename.description: The file name with its extension, e.g. "pricing.pdf". The extension decides the type.

annotations.title: Attach a file to a document

tools.name: remove_attachment
tools.description: Removes one attached file from a document. Readers lose the download from the next time they load the page. It removes the file only: the page, its links and its reading history are untouched, and there is no tool that deletes a page or a link. Claude cannot restore it, and it cannot be recovered from HTMLRadar, so attach it again from the original if the user changes their mind. Take the attachment id from list_attachments.

document_id.description: The document the file is attached to — from list_documents or list_shares.

annotations.title: Remove a file from a document

tools.name: get_reading_records
tools.description: Returns the reading records the HTMLRadar website exports as a spreadsheet, as CSV text: one row per section per read, with the link's label and address, the reader, whether their address was verified, when they opened it, how long they read, how far they scrolled, and their country and device where recorded. The sender's own previews and internal viewers are left out, as on the website. Pass `share_id` for one link; without it every link of the document is included. A very long answer is cut at a whole record and gives a `continue_from` value: call again with the same arguments and that value for the next rows, until it says it is every row. For a quick answer about who read one link, get_share_activity is shorter. It changes nothing.

document_id.description: The document — the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

share_id.description: Limit the records to one link: the share id, the share's slug, or the link itself.

continue_from.description: The `continue_from` value a previous answer gave, to read the rows after it. Omit it to start from the first row.

tools.name: replace_document
tools.description: Replaces the contents of a document already on HTMLRadar. Every existing link stays exactly as it is — same address, same settings, same reading history — and serves the new contents from the next time it is opened, so nobody is sent a second link. The new HTML is screened for phishing signals as every upload is, and the previous version stays listed in the document's version history on the website. Restoring an earlier version is not available, from Claude or on the website; to go back, replace the contents again with the earlier page. Recipients may already have read the old contents. Pass either the whole new page in `html`, or `edits`: pieces of text to find in the page get_document returned, each with its replacement and each appearing exactly once. Edits suit small changes to a large page, because only the changes travel. Images that need a login, expiring image addresses and local file paths do not load for readers of the link. Images embedded in the HTML as data URIs always do. On an update, get_document shows each embedded image as a short htmlradar-image reference; keep each one exactly as it is and HTMLRadar puts the image back, so only new images count towards the 5 MB limit.

announce.description: Tell readers what changed and alert subscribers. Omit to announce only when every live link is company-only; otherwise the replacement is quiet.

note.description: Optional note for an announced update, at most 140 characters.

document_id.description: The document whose contents are being replaced. Every link to it keeps working.

html.description: The new HTML markup, in full. It may keep the htmlradar-image references get_document returned. Pass this or `edits`, not both.

edits.description: Changes to the page get_document returned, applied in order. Each `find` must appear exactly once in the page at that point. Between 1 and 200. Pass this or `html`.

find.description: Text in the page or passages get_document returned, copied exactly; it must appear exactly once in the whole page.

replace.description: The text that takes its place.

expected_version.description: The document's current version as you last saw it: get_document and list_documents show it, and each replace_document result gives the new one. When the document has been replaced since, nothing is replaced and the call says so, so newer work is never overwritten.

request_id.description: Leave unset on a first attempt. When a previous call failed saying it may still have been applied, pass the request_id that error named: the retry then returns the first result instead of doing it twice.

annotations.title: Replace a document, keeping every link

tools.name: get_document
tools.description: Returns the current contents of a document on HTMLRadar so they can be changed and put back with replace_document. Each image embedded as a data URI appears as a short htmlradar-image reference instead of its data; keep references exactly as they are. A page over 5 MB of text even with its images as references is too large to read whole; with `query`, a word or phrase from the part to change, any page returns only the passages where that text appears, which replace_document `edits` can then change. It reads only this account's documents and changes nothing.

document_id.description: The document to read — the document id from list_documents or list_shares.

query.description: Text to find, 1 to 200 characters, matched literally with letter case ignored, such as a product name or a price. Returns up to 20 passages around the matches, and how many there are, instead of the whole page: the way to edit a page too large to read whole.

annotations.title: Read a document to change it

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Reports which HTMLRadar account the API key belongs to (its email address), the plan it is on and how many of its free tracked links remain.

annotations.title: Show the HTMLRadar plan and free links left

tools.name: get_page_guidelines
tools.description: Returns HTMLRadar's guidelines for pages that read well on phones and give accurate section reading

instructions: Use HTMLRadar when the user wants to send a web page, deck, report or dashboard to specific people, control who can open it, see how each person read it, and update it on the same link. Use share_html once you have produced a deck, report, dashboard, proposal or one-pager that the user intends to send to someone else, and get_share_activity when they ask whether it was read. When the user refers to something they sent earlier, call list_shares first to find its identifiers rather than asking them to look one up, and list_documents when what they mean has no link yet. create_share makes another link for a document that already exists, which is what "send this to these five people" needs; replace_document puts new contents behind links that have already been sent, so every reader sees the new version on the same link; get_document returns a document's current contents so they can be edited and put back with replace_document; revoke_share switches a link off, or back on; get_share reads a sent link's current settings and update_share changes them (who can open it, the email gate and code, the password, the end date, the copy lock) on the same link, so do not make a new link to change a setting; change one address or domain with the add and remove arguments, and pass get_share's settings version as expected_settings_version when replacing a whole list; list_attachments, add_attachment and remove_attachment manage the files attached to a document; and get_reading_records returns the same reading records the website exports. No tool deletes a page or a link: that is only on the website. On a free account, publishing spends one of a small number of tracked links — whoami says how many are left. If a publish is refused for that reason, say so and do not retry. If a call says it needs approval for new permissions, give the user the link and do not retry; they approve it in one click and stay connected. Ask the user before publishing, replacing, changing a setting, adding or removing a file, or revoking anything. When you write the page yourself, get_page_guidelines returns how to make it read well on phones and give accurate section reading.
